title: Egg Fried Rice
subtitle: Day-old rice stir-fried with eggs, soy sauce and spring onions
excerpt: Leftover rice is stir-fried in a very hot wok with beaten egg, soy sauce and spring onions until each grain is separate and lightly coated. The dish relies almost entirely on technique: the right rice, the right heat, and moving fast. Serves 4 in about 15 minutes.
sourceNotes: Fried rice is one of the oldest and most widespread dishes in Chinese cooking. Recipes appear in Yan-Kit So's 'Classic Food of China' (Macmillan, 1992) and the technique is discussed in detail in Fuchsia Dunlop's 'Every Grain of Rice' (Bloomsbury, 2012), which traces the practice of frying cold leftover rice to frugal household cooking across southern China and notes that using freshly cooked hot rice produces an inferior result.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the rice the day before and refrigerate uncovered for at least 4 hours so it dries out. This is not optional for good results.

glossaryTerms.definition: Cantonese for 'wok breath', the slightly smoky, caramelised flavour that develops when food is cooked at very high heat in a well-seasoned wok. It comes from the Maillard reaction between the hot metal and the food. A domestic hob produces less wok hei than a professional gas burner, but the effect can be improved by using the smallest wok that fits the quantity and getting it properly smoking before adding ingredients.

Rice that has been cooked, cooled and refrigerated for at least several hours, ideally overnight. Refrigeration dries the surface of each grain and reduces moisture content, which means the grains fry separately rather than clumping together or going mushy. Freshly cooked rice contains too much steam to fry well.

A thin, pale soy sauce with a clean, salty flavour used as a seasoning and table condiment. It is distinct from dark soy sauce, which is thicker, sweeter and used mainly for colour. For fried rice, light soy keeps the colour of the dish pale and golden rather than dark brown.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes about 15 minutes, not counting the overnight rest for the rice.
is not a suggestion: it is the only way to get separate, non-sticky grains. Plan ahead and cook extra rice the night before.
The wok must be hot before anything goes in. A properly heated wok is what creates

, the slightly smoky flavour that sets good fried rice apart from a reheated version. Open windows or turn on the extractor: the wok will smoke. Keep the heat high throughout and never add so much rice that the wok temperature drops significantly.
Break up any clumps in the cold {{cooked-jasmine-rice}} with your hands before cooking. Have all other ingredients ready and within reach.
Heat a wok over the highest heat on your hob until it begins to smoke. Add 2 tablespoons of the {{vegetable-oil}} and swirl to coat the sides.
Pour in the beaten {{eggs}} and leave for 10 seconds until the edges set, then scramble them loosely with a spatula. They should still be slightly underdone when you move to the next step.
Add the rice and remaining oil to the wok. Press the rice flat against the wok surface and leave for 30 seconds to toast, then toss and repeat. Keep the heat very high and keep the rice moving.
Add the peas if using. Stir-fry for 1 minute more until the peas are heated through and the rice smells toasted.
Add the {{light-soy-sauce}}, {{sesame-oil}} and white pepper. Toss thoroughly for 30 seconds. Add the {{spring-onions}}, toss once more and serve.

items.symptom: The rice is clumping and going mushy
items.cause: The rice was freshly cooked or still too moist
items.fix: Only use rice that has been refrigerated for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. If you must use fresh rice, spread it on a tray and cool it in the freezer for 30 minutes.

items.symptom: The fried rice is grey and bland
items.cause: The wok was not hot enough and no browning occurred
items.fix: The wok must be visibly smoking before the oil goes in. Use the highest heat your hob has and do not overcrowd the wok. Cook in two batches if needed.

items.symptom: The egg has disappeared into the rice
items.cause: The eggs were scrambled too finely before the rice went in
items.fix: Leave the eggs in larger soft curds before adding the rice. They will break up a little more as you toss, but visible egg pieces are what you want.

content.text: Egg fried rice is a household staple across China and much of East and Southeast Asia. In Chinese home cooking it is one of the primary ways to use up leftover rice, and the simplest version, with just egg, soy sauce and spring onion, is often considered the best test of a cook's wok technique.
